summary: The NEA opposes any reduction or sunset of the E‑Rate program, arguing it is essential for affordable broadband, equity, and sustaining connectivity for schools and libraries. They highlight the program’s role in bridging the digital divide, its ongoing operational cost coverage, and the high discounts for low‑income and rural institutions. NEA opposes sunset of E‑Rate and any limitation of service to rural or single‑provider areas, arguing the program remains essential for ongoing connectivity and equity. NEA argues against limiting E‑Rate to rural or low‑participation areas, cautions against tying support to participation rates, opposes conditioning broadband funding on screen‑time limits, insists Head‑Start and pre‑K remain eligible, and supports program integrity measures without undermining E‑Rate. NEA urges the FCC to strengthen program integrity while preserving the E‑Rate program, opposing sunset or narrowing of eligibility, and supporting targeted oversight of high‑disparity contracts.
